metadata.description: An outcome: a host's logs are shipped to a central sink, tagged with the host's identity. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): the OpenTelemetry Collector's source-to-sink contract (OTLP, Prometheus exposition) abstracts over every shipper, so a shipper with a given source, sink and labels is one deliverable any telemetry provider realizes. The consumer says which host and which sink and nothing about how; the mechanism (a configuration-management role, a job template, a container) is the provider's and swapping it never touches this contract.

target.description: The host whose logs are shipped; the shipper runs on or collects from it.

sink.description: Where the logs go: the central store's endpoint (an OTLP push URL). The store itself is another entity.

url.description: Log-store push endpoint (e.g. an OTLP push URL).

source.description: Which logs: the systemd journal (default) or on-disk files.

labels.description: Extra stream labels beyond the host and unit identity (environment, role).

status.description: Realized health of the shipper (e.g. running / degraded), as reported by discovery.

shipping_to.description: The sink URL the shipper is delivering to (echo of realized config).

last_shipped_at.description: OBSERVED — a provider-watched liveness fact, not derivable from model records (no shipment-instance records exist; this is heartbeat, not history). Timestamp of the most recent successful delivery (RFC 3339) — drives drift / staleness detection.

context.purpose: Declares the outcome that a host's logs reach the central sink — without saying anything about how.
context.plain_description: A statement of outcome: logs from a target host — the `target` object naming its `host` — shipped to a named sink URL — the `sink` object carrying its `url`; both are objects, not flat strings — tagged with the host's identity. The consumer never sees the mechanism — whether a provider satisfies it with an automation-managed agent, a container, or something else is the provider's private business, and swapping mechanisms changes nothing in this record. Realized state reports whether shipping is healthy and when the last successful delivery happened, which drives staleness detection.
use_when: You need logs-from-host-X-land-in-the-central-store as a declared, checkable fact per host.
You need shipping health and last-delivery time surfaced for drift and staleness detection.
not_for: The log store itself — that is its own resource (e.g. a Workload running the sink); this type is the per-host shipping outcome.
Metrics or trace collection — not covered; this type is logs.
works_with: Machine.BareMetalHost / Machine.VM — the target host whose logs are shipped.
Workload — the central log store the sink URL points at.
